name: Mountain Pose (Tadasana)
benefits: Improves posture, balance, and body awareness. Gentle grounding pose that builds attention to alignment.
contraindications: None significant. Safe for essentially all practitioners, including those with knee or back injuries, since it is a static standing pose with no bending or loading.
description: Stand with feet hip-width apart, weight even across both feet, arms relaxed at sides, spine long, gaze forward.

name: Child's Pose (Balasana)
benefits: Gently stretches the back, hips, and thighs. Calming, often used to rest between more active poses.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with knee injury, since the pose folds the knees fully and places body weight over them; a cushion under the knees or a wide-knee variation reduces load. Avoid deep forward compression during pregnancy.
description: Kneel, sit back onto the heels, fold the torso forward over the thighs, arms extended or relaxed alongside the body.

name: Cat-Cow (Marjaryasana-Bitilasana)
benefits: Warms up the spine, improves spinal mobility and coordination with breath.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with wrist injury, since it bears weight through the wrists; fists or forearms can substitute. Keep the neck neutral if there is neck injury or strain.
description: On hands and knees, alternate between arching the spine (cow) and rounding it (cat), moving with the breath.

name: Downward-Facing Dog (Adho Mukha Svanasana)
benefits: Stretches hamstrings and calves, strengthens arms and shoulders, mildly inverts the body to encourage circulation.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with wrist injury or carpal tunnel due to sustained weight-bearing on the hands. Use caution with high blood pressure because the head is below the heart.
description: From hands and knees, lift the hips up and back, forming an inverted V with straight arms and legs.

name: Warrior I (Virabhadrasana I)
benefits: Strengthens the legs and core, opens the hips and chest, builds stamina.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with knee injury, since the front knee bends deeply and bears significant load; keep the bend shallow or use a shorter stance. Use caution with high blood pressure when raising the arms overhead.
description: Step one foot back, square the hips forward, bend the front knee to roughly 90 degrees, raise both arms overhead.

name: Warrior II (Virabhadrasana II)
benefits: Builds leg strength and stamina, opens the hips, improves focus and stability.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with knee injury, since the front knee holds a deep bend under sustained load; shallow the bend or shorten the stance.
description: Step the feet wide apart, turn the front foot out, bend the front knee over the ankle, extend arms parallel to the floor.

name: Triangle Pose (Trikonasana)
benefits: Stretches the legs, hips, and spine, improves balance and lateral flexibility.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with neck injury when turning the gaze upward; keep the neck neutral instead. Use caution with low back injury.
description: Stand with feet wide, extend the torso sideways over the front leg, reaching the front hand toward the shin or floor and the back hand toward the ceiling.

name: Tree Pose (Vrksasana)
benefits: Improves balance and concentration, strengthens the standing leg and ankle.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with knee injury on the standing leg, since balancing concentrates load through that knee; place the lifted foot below the knee (on the calf or ankle) rather than pressing directly on the knee joint.
description: Balance on one leg, place the sole of the other foot on the inner calf or thigh, hands at heart center or overhead.

name: Chair Pose (Utkatasana)
benefits: Strengthens the thighs, glutes, and core, builds heat and stamina.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with knee injury due to the sustained deep knee bend; a shallower bend reduces joint load. Use caution with low back issues.
description: Bend the knees and sink the hips back as if sitting into a chair, arms raised overhead, weight in the heels.

name: Bridge Pose (Setu Bandhasana)
benefits: Strengthens the back and glutes, gently opens the chest, a knee-safe alternative to standing backbends since it is performed lying down with no weight on the knees.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with neck injury, since the pose loads the back of the neck and shoulders.
description: Lie on the back, feet flat and hip-width apart, lift the hips while pressing through the feet and shoulders.

name: Cobra Pose (Bhujangasana)
benefits: Strengthens the spine, opens the chest and shoulders, gentle backbend.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with wrist injury, since the hands bear weight to lift the chest. Use caution with pregnancy or significant low back injury.
description: Lie face down, hands under the shoulders, press the chest up while keeping the hips grounded.

name: Seated Forward Fold (Paschimottanasana)
benefits: Stretches the hamstrings and spine, calming and introspective.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with low back injury; bending the knees slightly reduces strain on the lower back.
description: Sit with legs extended, fold the torso forward over the legs, reaching toward the feet.

name: Legs-Up-The-Wall (Viparita Karani)
benefits: Relieves tired legs, promotes circulation and relaxation, effective for stress relief. Knee-safe since the legs rest passively against a wall with no standing or bearing weight.
contraindications: Avoid with glaucoma or other serious eye pressure conditions.
description: Lie on the back with the legs extended up a wall, arms relaxed at the sides, staying passive and breathing slowly.

name: Corpse Pose (Savasana)
benefits: Deep relaxation, integrates the effects of practice, calms the nervous system. Knee-safe, as it is performed lying flat with no joint loading at all.
contraindications: None significant. Safe for essentially all practitioners, including those with knee, back, or joint injuries.
description: Lie flat on the back, arms and legs relaxed and slightly apart, eyes closed, breathing naturally.

name: Easy Pose (Sukhasana)
benefits: Calms the mind, gently opens the hips, supports breathing and meditation practice.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with knee injury, since sitting cross-legged loads the knee joints; sitting on a cushion or using a chair instead removes that load.
description: Sit cross-legged with a tall spine, hands resting on the knees or in the lap, breathing steadily.

name: Standing Forward Fold (Uttanasana)
benefits: Stretches the hamstrings and calves, calms the nervous system.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with low back injury; bend the knees generously to reduce strain. Use caution with high blood pressure due to the inverted head position.
description: From standing, hinge at the hips and fold the torso forward, letting the head hang, knees soft.

name: Plank Pose
benefits: Builds core and arm strength, improves overall stability.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with wrist injury or shoulder injury, since the pose bears full body weight through the hands and shoulders.
description: Hold a straight line from head to heels, supported on the hands and toes, core engaged.

name: Camel Pose (Ustrasana)
benefits: Deep backbend that opens the chest and shoulders and strengthens the back.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with knee injury, since the pose is performed kneeling with body weight on the knees. Use caution with low back or neck injury.
description: Kneel with hips over knees, arch the back and reach the hands toward the heels, chest lifted.

name: Reclining Bound Angle Pose (Supta Baddha Konasana)
benefits: Gently opens the hips, restorative and relaxing. Knee-safe, since the pose is reclined and supported, with no weight bearing on the knees.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with groin or hip injury.
description: Lie on the back, bring the soles of the feet together and let the knees fall open to the sides, supported with cushions if needed.

name: Pigeon Pose (Eka Pada Rajakapotasana)
benefits: Deep hip opener, releases tension held in the hips and glutes.
contraindications: Avoid or modify with knee injury, since the front leg's bent position places rotational stress on the knee joint. Use caution with hip injury.
description: From hands and knees, bring one knee forward toward the same-side wrist, extend the other leg straight back, fold forward if comfortable.
